key_insight: Fusing diverse synthetic license-plate images with real, multinational data substantially improves OCR robustness and cross-country generalization for license plate recognition models; a large-scale benchmark identifies which models and mixing strategies benefit most.
problem_solved: Addresses the scarcity and heterogeneity of annotated multinational license-plate data and the limited understanding of how to best combine synthetic and real images to boost LPR performance across different countries and plate styles.
method: Generate diverse synthetic license-plate images that capture multinational layout, font, color and environmental variations.
Combine (fuse) synthetic and real datasets and train/evaluate 16 OCR models across 12 public datasets to measure performance gains.
Run systematic benchmarking and ablation analyses to quantify the effect of different mixing ratios, augmentation choices, and model architectures on recognition accuracy.
impact: Provides practical guidance to reduce costly annotation needs and improve real-world, cross-border LPR performance; helps practitioners choose architectures and data-mixing strategies that maximize accuracy and generalization.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing synthetic data generation → data fusion → OCR training → evaluation
Bar/line charts comparing OCR accuracy across the 16 models and 12 datasets (with/without synthetic data)
World map overlay indicating dataset coverage and plate-style variations by region
Ablation table/heatmap showing performance vs. synthetic:real mixing ratios and key augmentation choices
paper_title: Advancing Multinational License Plate Recognition Through Synthetic and Real Data Fusion: A Comprehensive Evaluation
paper_authors: Rayson Laroca, Valter Estevam, Gladston J. P. Moreira, Rodrigo Minetto, David Menotti
